headline: WORLD'S BIGGEST COPPER MINE SLOWLY RESTARTS — Escondida Begins Phased Return After Fatal Sept 23 Accident; Sernageomin Investigation Underway
snippet: BHP's Escondida mine — the world's largest copper producer at 1.3 million tonnes/year — began a gradual phased resumption of operations on September 24-25 after a fatal contractor accident on September 23 involving a front-end loader during maintenance work. Chile's national regulator Sernageomin deployed its Antofagasta regional team to investigate; Chilean law requires inspector sign-off before full restart. The partial resumption eases but does not eliminate the supply disruption that briefly supported the LME copper rally to a record $14,875/MT on September 22.

headline: GOLD DROPS TO $4,250, SILVER UNDER $63 — Fed at 3.75%, 10-Year Treasury Hits 5.12%; October Hike at 67% Odds; Dollar Near 2-Month High
snippet: Gold retreated to $4,250-$4,291 on September 25 — dropping below the $4,300 level the prior week's bullish commentary anchored on — as the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in three years (to 3.75%-4.00%) combined with a 10-year Treasury yield reaching 5.12% (highest since 2007) and the dollar climbing to a near two-month high. Markets are pricing a 67% probability of an October follow-up hike. Silver slid 1.36% to $63.45 on Thursday and extended losses Friday, with COMEX registered silver stocks at 96.3 million ounces and drifting lower. Gold remains 23% off January's $5,595 record; if yields hold, the near-term path stays choppy despite record producer margins.

headline: CYGNUS SHAREHOLDERS GREEN-LIGHT CENTRAL ASIA METALS DEAL — A$232M All-Share Takeover Adds Chibougamau Copper-Gold to AIM-Listed Portfolio
snippet: Cygnus Metals (ASX: CY5) shareholders voted September 24 to approve the scheme of arrangement under which Central Asia Metals (AIM: CAML) acquires 100% of Cygnus in an all-share transaction valued at approximately A$232 million, adding the Chibougamau copper-gold project in Quebec to CAML's Kazakh and North Macedonian asset base. A Western Australian Supreme Court hearing formalised the scheme on September 23; a Kazakhstan regulatory approval condition remains outstanding before the deal closes. The combined entity splits approximately 70% legacy CAML shareholders and 30% Cygnus holders — the latest in a pattern of AIM-listed UK miners acquiring junior assets in North American critical minerals jurisdictions.

headline: 68m AT 0.62% Cu, 1.44% Zn NEAR-SURFACE — Litchfield Gains 12.5% on Oonagalabi Result; BHP Xplor Backing Accelerates NT Copper-Zinc Play
snippet: Litchfield Minerals (ASX: LMS) jumped 12.5% on September 24 after Phase 3 drilling at Oonagalabi in the Northern Territory returned 68.26 metres at 0.62% Cu, 1.44% Zn, and 4.3 g/t Ag — with a near-surface southwest intercept starting at 2 metres depth. The company has mapped a 5km mineralised copper-zinc corridor and was accepted into BHP's elite 2026 Xplor accelerator program, providing non-dilutive funding and expert guidance. With follow-up drilling scheduled next month via Topdrill, Oonagalabi is emerging as one of Australia's more significant near-surface polymetallic discoveries of the current cycle.

headline: 46 g/t AU OVER 1.9m IN 7.88 g/t HALO — Dryden Confirms 350m High-Grade Strike at Gold Rock; Second Rig Drilling Down-Plunge at 330m Depth
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp (TSXV: DRY) announced September 23 that drill hole DGR-058 at Gold Rock, Ontario returned 7.88 g/t Au over 12.70 metres — including a 46.05 g/t Au sub-interval over 1.90 metres — filling the gap between the Jubilee and Pearl high-grade zones and confirming continuous high-grade mineralisation over approximately 350 metres of the Elora structure. A second drill rig added in July hit 9.40 g/t Au over 4.60 metres at 330 metres true depth on August 31, suggesting both near-surface grades and open down-plunge potential. The 2025-2026 campaign has expanded Gold Rock from 3 to 15 mineralised structures across the property.

headline: GLENCORE LOCKS UP RECYCLED LITHIUM — $1B, 10-Year "Project SHIELD" Offtake; 24,000t/yr Black Mass In, Battery-Grade Lithium Carbonate + Nickel MHP Out
snippet: Nth Cycle and Glencore signed a binding term sheet on September 22 representing an estimated $1 billion over 10 years for Project SHIELD — a US battery materials refinery planned for South Carolina that will receive 100% of the black mass from Glencore's commercial network and operating US shredding assets (24,000 tonnes/year), in exchange for offtake of Nth Cycle's high-purity mixed hydroxide product and battery-grade lithium carbonate. Announced at the UN General Assembly ahead of an Nth Cycle IPO, the deal follows a separate 12,000 tonne/year Trafigura offtake signed in March 2026 and represents one of the largest integrated battery recycling partnerships in North American history.

headline: $7 BILLION IN US EXPORT CREDIT TARGETS ARGENTINA — EXIM Bank to Finance Lithium, Copper, Rare Earths Under Milei's Mineral Deal; Mining Minister Targets 5x Export Surge by 2036
snippet: The US Export-Import Bank announced at the UN General Assembly on September 22 that it will make up to $7 billion available for critical minerals and energy projects in Argentina over two years, allowing companies to purchase US equipment for lithium, copper, and rare earth development under the February 2026 bilateral framework signed with President Milei. Argentina's mining minister has projected the country could increase lithium exports to 580,000 metric tonnes/year and copper exports to 1.64 million metric tonnes/year by 2036 — five times 2025 levels. The announcement substantially lowers sovereign and financing risk for junior and mid-tier miners operating in the Lithium Triangle, where the US backing effectively replaces a previous funding vacuum.

headline: GREENLAND PACT BARS CHINA FROM RARE EARTH ASSETS — Critical Metals +25%, Tanbreez Exploitation Licence Worth $4.5B NPV; Greenland Mines Surges 200%
snippet: The US-Denmark-Greenland security pact that bars adversary-nation investments without US approval triggered a sharp rally in Greenland-linked rare earth names the week of September 21: Critical Metals (Nasdaq: CRML) surged 25% as the market priced its Tanbreez project — Greenland's only operational rare earth exploitation licence — as a Western strategic supply asset, with preliminary modelling showing $4.5B NPV10 for a proposed Romanian joint-venture refinery processing 100,000 tonnes/year of eudialyte into 19 high-purity products at $1.85B capital cost. Greenland Mines surged 200% and MP Materials, USA Rare Earth also gained. The moves complement China-side pressure building ahead of Beijing's November 10 export controls deadline.

headline: URANIUM TERM CONTRACTS HIT RECORD $96.50/lb — Kazatomprom Cuts Quota 8M lbs AND Signals No Spot Price Will Prompt Expansion; Spot at $89.55/lb
snippet: Uranium long-term contract prices reached a record $96.50/lb as of September 10 — surpassing the 2007 peak — while spot uranium stood at $89.55/lb as of September 23, with Kazatomprom compounding the supply picture by cutting its nominal 2026 production quota by 8 million pounds to approximately 77 million pounds and stating in September that no spot price level would prompt accelerated or expanded output. The structure of the uranium forward curve now shows term prices above spot, a signal that utilities contracting years ahead have concluded the structural supply deficit is durable — a thesis Cameco also underpinned by cutting McArthur River guidance.

headline: GOGOLD LOS RICOS SOUTH: 150 CONTRACTORS ON SITE, $284M CASH, ZERO DEBT — Plant Design 90% Complete; SAG Mill Arriving May 2027 for Q2 2028 Silver Pour
snippet: GoGold Resources (TSX: GGD) provided a September 22 construction update on Los Ricos South in Jalisco, Mexico confirming the project remains on schedule: site clearing is well advanced with 150+ contractors on site, all long-lead equipment orders are placed, plant design is 90% complete, and underground contractor Cominvi will mobilize in Q4 2026. Key milestones include powerline installation in November 2026, major concrete works and underground development starting January 2027, SAG mill delivery May 2027, and first silver pour target of Q2 2028. The project is fully funded with US$284 million cash and strong cash flow from Parral, requiring zero new equity; maximum cash outlay in Q3 2027 still preserves a $130 million minimum reserve.

headline: 166 g/t AU AND 3,383 g/t AG OVER 3.1m AT PREMIER — Cambria Gold Mines Expands BC Discovery; First Results from Silver Coin Due October
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines announced September 22 highlight drill intervals at its Premier Gold Project in British Columbia that include 166.22 g/t Au and 3,383 g/t Ag over 3.1 metres — exceptional bonanza-grade silver numbers that, combined with the gold grade, add to Premier's status as a high-priority drill target in one of Canada's most productive precious metals districts. The company's expanded drill program continues through year-end 2026 with initial results from the adjacent Silver Coin target expected in October, where successful results could substantially re-rate the combined land position.
